item.title: Media’s Morning Brief — October 01, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, here is Media’s Morning Brief.
Hundreds of college radio stations around the world come together Friday for the 16th annual World College Radio Day. More than 40 countries now celebrate the event. Media Jobs Report supports future media professionals year-round with free internship search, scholarship search, airplay charts and real-world industry tools at MediaJobsReport.com.
Turning to digital media, California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed SB 690, changing the state’s Invasion of Privacy Act. The News/Media Alliance says the measure gives publishers greater protection from lawsuits involving commonly used website technologies while preserving California privacy protections.
Turning to radio, Townsquare Media is expanding its digital advertising partnerships. The company has signed a deal with Lakes Media Network, giving its six radio brands in Virginia and North Carolina access to Townsquare Ignite’s programmatic advertising, audience targeting and performance reporting technology.
In radio news, Nine PBS has been awarded more than $11 million in first-year federal Ready To Learn funding. The station will lead the new Everyday Literacy Alliance, expand Teaching in Room 9 nationally, and partner with Fred Rogers Productions on a new preschool literacy program called Fredosaurus Rex.
Turning to media careers, Universal Music Group is expanding Frank Briegmann’s international leadership role. Briegmann has been promoted to Chairman and CEO of Universal Music Europe, Australia, New Zealand, Canada and Deutsche Grammophon. UMG says the new structure is designed to increase collaboration across markets and create more opportunities for local artists to reach audiences worldwide. Briegmann joined Universal Music in 2004 and will continue reporting to Chairman and CEO Sir Lucian Grainge.
In media jobs, TikTok supported an estimated $81 billion in U.S. GDP and 410,000 American jobs in 2025, according to a new PF Global report. The study also found TikTok discovery generated $4.7 billion in local spending, while 93% of businesses surveyed reported increased sales after promoting on the platform.
From the radio side of the industry, From Miami, iHeartMedia is kicking off its 2026 Fiesta Latina celebration with a free party at the Miami Design District on October 15. Enrique Santos and Dayanara Torres will host the event, featuring Tony Succar’s Unity: The Latin Tribute to Michael Jackson, along with Jean Rodriguez, Anthony Ramos and Backstreet Boys member Howie D. The celebration leads into the main iHeartRadio Fiesta Latina concert on October 17 at Kaseya Center, featuring Anuel AA, Myke Towers, Farruko, Manuel Turizo and more. Lin-Manuel Miranda will also receive the 2026 iHeartRadio Corazón Latino Award.
And finally, Sounds Profitable’s Podcast Landscape 2026 finds podcast reach holding steady, with 74% of U.S. adults having consumed a podcast. Video continues to grow, while Netflix has emerged as the third most-named podcast platform behind YouTube and Spotify.
For more media headlines, jobs, tools and industry information, visit Media Jobs Report dot com.
